query: For nanoparticles composed of five or more metals in equal or near-equal atomic ratios and initially crystallized as a solid solution, what governs whether structural and chemical stability is maintained across catalytic and thermoelectric operating ranges of 473–1923 K? Formulate one testable mechanistic hypothesis, specify a controlled comparison, predict observations relative to the initial baseline, define the conditions under which the prediction should hold, identify supporting evidence, and state a result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: For equiatomic (or near-equiatomic) nanoparticles composed of five or more metals and initially crystallized as a single-phase solid solution, maintenance of structural (single-phase lattice) and chemical (near-uniform composition) stability across 473–1923 K is governed by the competition between bulk configurational stabilization and surface/chemical segregation driving forces. Specifically, stability is achieved when the variance of binary mixing enthalpies among the constituent pairs is low and the spread in elemental surface energies (and oxide formation enthalpies under the working atmosphere) is small. In this regime, configurational entropy and modest, uniformly negative mixing enthalpy suppress demixing, while limited surface-energy contrast reduces segregation; lattice distortion further slows diffusion. If the spread in oxide formation enthalpy is large in oxidizing atmospheres, selective surface segregation of the most oxophilic element occurs, destabilizing the solid solution even if it is stable in inert/reducing atmospheres.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic 5–7 component alloy nanoparticles (8 ± 2 nm diameter) synthesized as a single-phase FCC or BCC solid solution, compositionally uniform within ±5 at.% radially, clean metallic surface (no detectable surface oxide), supported on inert SiO2.
generation.intervention: Thermal exposure across 473–1923 K under controlled atmospheres (Ar, 5% H2/Ar, 20% O2/Ar, and reactive feeds such as CO/CO2/H2O) with staged isothermal holds and ramps.
generation.conditions: Heat at 10 K/min to isotherms corresponding to 0.4, 0.6, and 0.7 of the composition-weighted average melting temperature (T_m,avg), hold 2 h at each step; total pressure 1 bar; particle size 8 ± 2 nm; inert SiO2 support; gas compositions as stated. Note: for typical HEA compositions, 0.4–0.7 T_m,avg often spans within 473–1500 K; above ~0.8 T_m,avg (potentially approaching 1923 K for some alloys) behavior may deviate due to sintering/melting.
generation.structural_mediator: Three linked descriptors: (1) the standard deviation of binary mixing enthalpies among all constituent pairs, sigma(ΔH_mix); (2) the spread in elemental surface energies, Δγ_surf; and (3) the spread in oxide formation enthalpies under the operating atmosphere, ΔH_ox,spread, with lattice distortion (atomic size mismatch, δ) moderating diffusion kinetics.
generation.mechanism: When sigma(ΔH_mix) is small and the average ΔH_mix is mildly negative, the enthalpic penalty for local demixing is low and is outweighed by configurational entropy, preserving a single-phase bulk lattice. A small Δγ_surf reduces the thermodynamic driving force for preferential surface segregation among constituents, keeping surface and bulk compositions aligned. A larger atomic size mismatch (δ) elevates activation barriers for surface and bulk diffusion, slowing coarsening and phase separation kinetics. In oxidizing atmospheres, elements with substantially more negative oxide formation enthalpy lower the surface free energy by segregating and oxidizing; a large ΔH_ox,spread therefore promotes selective surface enrichment and core depletion of the most oxophilic element, which can nucleate phase separation or core–shell structures.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compositions with sigma(ΔH_mix) ≤ ~5 kJ/mol, Δγ_surf ≤ ~0.3 J m^-2, δ ≥ ~5%, and ΔH_ox,spread ≤ ~50 kJ/mol will retain a single-phase lattice and near-uniform composition up to ~0.6–0.7 T_m,avg in Ar or 5% H2/Ar: (i) XRD remains single-phase (no new peaks) with peak shifts < ~0.2% relative to room temperature extrapolation, (ii) STEM-EDS/EELS radial profiles show deviations from equiatomic composition < ±5 at.% from core to surface, and (iii) no secondary phases in HR-TEM. Under 20% O2/Ar at ~0.6 T_m,avg: if ΔH_ox,spread > ~100 kJ/mol, the most oxophilic element exhibits selective surface enrichment by > ~15 at.% relative to the core and detectable core depletion, possibly with a thin oxide shell; if ΔH_ox,spread ≤ ~50 kJ/mol, surface enrichment remains within ±5 at.% and the single-phase metallic lattice is largely retained beneath any ultrathin oxide.
generation.baseline: Room-temperature state before thermal exposure: single-phase solid solution with equiatomic composition (±5 at.% radially), no segregated shells, no secondary phases; mean particle diameter 8 ± 2 nm.
generation.boundary: Prediction holds for 5–10 nm particles on inert supports without strong metal–support interactions, no highly volatile constituents, and absence of bulk compound formation (e.g., carbides/nitrides) under the chosen gases. Above ~0.8 T_m,avg (often approaching the upper end of 1923 K) or under strongly reactive feeds that form stable bulk compounds, sintering, melting, or compound formation can dominate and invalidate the stability criteria.
generation.uncertainty: Quantitative thresholds for sigma(ΔH_mix), Δγ_surf, δ, and ΔH_ox,spread are approximate and composition-dependent; effective T_m,avg for multicomponent nanoparticles is an approximation; support interactions, particle size dispersion, and true diffusivities can shift stability windows. The extent to which lattice distortion yields diffusional sluggishness is debated and may vary with phase (FCC vs BCC) and composition.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize two equiatomic 5-metal nanoparticle sets (8 ± 2 nm) with similar size and phase at room temperature but contrasting thermodynamic descriptors computed from accepted semi-empirical models: Set A with low sigma(ΔH_mix) (≤ ~5 kJ/mol), small Δγ_surf (≤ ~0.3 J m^-2), δ ≥ ~5%, and small ΔH_ox,spread (≤ ~50 kJ/mol); Set B with high sigma(ΔH_mix) (≥ ~10–15 kJ/mol), large Δγ_surf (≥ ~0.6 J m^-2), and inclusion of one strongly oxophilic element producing ΔH_ox,spread ≥ ~100 kJ/mol. Verify both sets are single-phase and equiatomic at baseline. Perform identical in situ thermal treatments in Ar, 5% H2/Ar, and 20% O2/Ar at 0.4, 0.6, and 0.7 T_m,avg (2 h holds).
measurements: In situ XRD for phase evolution and lattice parameter shifts
In situ or ex situ aberration-corrected STEM-HAADF with EDS/EELS for radial composition profiles (core vs surface)
XPS for surface composition and oxidation states
Particle size distributions (TEM) to monitor sintering
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if any of the following are observed: (1) Set A exhibits phase separation (new XRD peaks) or >10 at.% surface enrichment of any element relative to the core at or below 0.6 T_m,avg in Ar or 5% H2/Ar; (2) Set B remains single-phase and compositionally uniform within ±5 at.% up to 0.7 T_m,avg in Ar or 5% H2/Ar; (3) Under 20% O2/Ar at ~0.6 T_m,avg, a composition with ΔH_ox,spread ≥ ~100 kJ/mol fails to show selective surface enrichment (>15 at.%) of the most oxophilic element relative to the core.
